question: If take-off was inadvertently made with the canopy in the cooling-gap position, what should the pilot do?

options.text: Land the airplane and close the canopy on the ground — do not attempt to close it in flight
Close the canopy in flight once above 117 KIAS
Open the emergency windows to equalize pressure, then close the canopy
Continue the flight normally; the cooling-gap position has no effect on handling

explanation: AFM 4B.2 directs landing with the canopy in the cooling-gap position rather than attempting to close it in flight.

question: If RPM is indicating high (outside the green range), what is the first response?

options.text: Open ALTERNATE AIR on both engines
Reduce power of the affected engine and keep RPM within the green range using the power lever
Immediately feather the affected engine
Switch the VOTER to the opposite ECU

explanation: AFM 4B.3.1: for high RPM, reduce power on the affected engine and use the power lever to stay within the green range; if this fails, refer to 3.12.3.

question: During an extended descent from high altitude at low power, coolant temperature may decrease. What helps restore it to the green range?

options.text: Switching to the auxiliary fuel pump
Opening ALTERNATE AIR
An increase in power and a decrease in airspeed
A decrease in power and an increase in airspeed

explanation: AFM 4B.3.2(b): low coolant temperature during a low-power descent is corrected by increasing power and decreasing airspeed.

question: If oil pressure and coolant temperature are both within the green range but oil pressure indicates HIGH, what should be suspected?

options.text: An imminent total loss of oil
A stuck fuel selector valve
A failed gearbox oil pump
A false oil pressure indication — keep monitoring the temperatures

explanation: AFM 4B.3.4(a): if temperatures are normal despite a high oil pressure reading, a false indication should be suspected and temperatures should continue to be monitored.

question: At low oil temperatures, high oil pressure can sometimes occur. What is the recommended response?

options.text: Reduce the power setting until the warning disappears, and continue the warm-up at that reduced setting
Immediately shut down and feather the engine
Ignore it — the warning always clears itself within a minute
Switch to the opposite ECU using the VOTER switch

explanation: A note under AFM 4B.3.4 explains this combination can occur at low oil temperatures and recommends reducing power until the warning clears.

question: Below what usable fuel quantity does the L/R FUEL LOW caution message appear on the G1000?

options.text: 13.2 US gal
4 ± 1 US gal
1 US gal
10 US gal

explanation: AFM 7.10.3 states the L/R FUEL LOW caution activates when usable fuel in a main tank is below 4 ± 1 US gal.

question: If the L/R FUEL LOW caution is triggered purely by un-coordinated flight, what is the corrective action?

options.text: Increase bank angle to re-center the fuel over the pickup
Feather the affected engine as a precaution
Return to coordinated flight — not more than about half a ball sideslip, 3°-5° bank
Immediately switch to the auxiliary fuel tank

explanation: AFM 4B.4.4 explains the indication is calibrated for straight and level flight, and can be triggered by uncoordinated turns; the fix is to return to coordinated flight.

question: Below what bus voltage does the L/R VOLTS LOW caution illuminate?

options.text: Less than 24.1 Volts
Less than 20 Volts
Less than 28 Volts
Less than 25 Volts

explanation: AFM 4B.4.5/7.10.3 give the L/R VOLTS LOW threshold as bus voltage below 25 Volts.

question: If ONE alternator fails, what is the correct response for that alternator's switch?

options.text: Set the ALTERNATOR switch OFF on the affected side, monitor bus voltage, and reduce electrical consumers as practicable
Leave the ALTERNATOR switch ON to attempt self-recovery
Immediately switch OFF both alternators as a precaution
Cycle the ALTERNATOR switch every 30 seconds

explanation: AFM 4B.4.6(a): with one alternator failed, switch it OFF, monitor bus voltage, and reduce electrical load as practicable.

question: At what engine compartment temperature does the fire detection system trigger a warning?

options.text: Above 400 °C (752 °F)
Above 250 °C (480 °F)
Above 105 °C (221 °F)
Above 140 °C (284 °F)

explanation: AFM 7.9.9: the overheat detector closes its circuit and triggers a fire warning above 250 °C (480 °F) in the engine compartment.

question: What system failure mode causes the STICK LIMIT caution to make the variable elevator backstop inoperative entirely, degrading power-on stall characteristics?

options.text: Both power levers at IDLE
The landing gear extended with flaps UP
Both power levers positioned above approximately 20% LOAD
At least one power lever below approximately 20% LOAD

explanation: AFM 4B.4.11(a): with both power levers above ~20% LOAD, the backstop is inoperative and stall characteristics are significantly degraded — the airplane must not be stalled in any configuration.

question: With STICK LIMIT active because at least one power lever is below approximately 20% LOAD, what airspeed must not be reduced below during approach?

options.text: vMCA (71 or 68 KIAS)
vYSE (85 KIAS)
vNO (151 KIAS)
vREF (84 KIAS up to 1900 kg, 86 KIAS above 1900 kg)

explanation: AFM 4B.4.11(b): with reduced elevator authority, airspeed must not go below vREF (84/86 KIAS) during the landing approach, especially with a forward CG.

question: When does the CHECK GEAR caution message appear?

options.text: When either the flaps are in LDG position, or one power lever is below approximately 20% LOAD, while the gear is not down and locked
Only when the flaps reach the LDG position, regardless of power
Only when both power levers are below 20% LOAD
Whenever the gear selector is moved, regardless of gear position

explanation: AFM 4B.4.12 explains CHECK GEAR triggers under either flaps-LDG or low-power-lever conditions if the gear is not down and locked.

question: If the LOI (loss of integrity) annunciation appears on final approach, what should the pilot do?

options.text: Ignore it — LOI is advisory only on final approach
Abort GPS-based navigation for that approach
Continue the approach and verify position every 15 minutes
Switch to the standby GPS receiver and continue

explanation: AFM 4B.4.13(b): on final approach, an LOI annunciation means GPS-based navigation must be aborted; away from final approach, position is instead verified every 15 minutes using another means.

question: If only the UP flap position is available due to a flap system failure, what is the minimum approach airspeed?

options.text: 90 KIAS
71 KIAS
86 KIAS
84 KIAS

explanation: AFM 4B.5(a): with only UP flaps available, the minimum approach airspeed is 86 KIAS, versus 84 KIAS if only APP is available.

question: If a flap system failure leaves only the flaps in APP position available, what is the minimum approach airspeed?

options.text: 86 KIAS
88 KIAS
90 KIAS
84 KIAS

explanation: AFM 4B.5(b): with only APP available, the minimum approach airspeed is 84 KIAS, versus 86 KIAS if only UP is available.

question: If a flap position or function failure occurs, what maximum airspeed keeps the airplane within the white arc?

options.text: 113 KIAS
133 KIAS
151 KIAS
122 KIAS

explanation: AFM 4B.5 directs keeping airspeed in the white sector, maximum 113 KIAS, while troubleshooting a flap indication or function failure.

question: What indicates continuous or intermittent hydraulic pump operation as an abnormal condition requiring preparation for manual gear extension?

options.text: The pump running only during actual gear cycling
The gear pump running continuously or periodically instead of stopping once system pressure is restored
The gear taking longer than 6 seconds to extend
A single 5-20 second pump run immediately after ELECT. MASTER is switched ON

explanation: AFM 4B.7.1 identifies continuous or periodic (rather than a single brief) pump operation as abnormal, since it indicates decreasing system pressure and calls for preparing a manual gear extension.

question: What is the normal duration of hydraulic pump operation when ELECT. MASTER is first switched ON?

options.text: Exactly 60 seconds every time
It never runs automatically on ELECT. MASTER ON
5 to 20 seconds, to restore system pressure
Continuously, for as long as ELECT. MASTER stays ON

explanation: AFM 4A.6.1/4B.7.1 both note the hydraulic pump may run for 5-20 seconds when ELECT. MASTER is switched ON, restoring system pressure; continuous or periodic running beyond that indicates a malfunction.

question: When starting an engine with external power, which side is started first?

options.text: The RH engine
Whichever side has the coldest oil temperature
Both engines simultaneously
The LH engine

explanation: AFM 4B.8.2 starts the LH engine first with external power connected, then disconnects external power before starting the RH engine normally.

question: During an external-power start, at what ambient temperature might the engine not run on the first attempt?

options.text: Below -20 °C
Below -22 °C
Below 0 °C
Below -30 °C

explanation: AFM 4B.8.2 gives a slightly different threshold for external-power starts (-20 °C) than the normal-procedure start caution (-22 °C in AFM 4A.6.3).

question: During a lightning strike, what airspeed limit should not be exceeded?

options.text: vMCA (71 KIAS)
vO (operating maneuvering speed), refer to Section 2.2
vNE (188 KIAS)
vNO (151 KIAS)

explanation: AFM 4B.9 directs keeping airspeed as low as practicable, not exceeding vO, following a lightning strike.

question: What is the recommended maximum autopilot operating airspeed referenced during AUTOPILOT OVERSPEED RECOVERY?

options.text: 151 KIAS
165 KIAS
180 KIAS
188 KIAS

explanation: AFM 4B.10.2 explains the overspeed recovery pitches up to decelerate the airplane at or below the 180 KIAS maximum autopilot operating speed.

question: If a navigation signal is lost while the autopilot is tracking it, what does the autopilot do automatically?

options.text: Disconnect entirely with no default mode
Continue tracking the last known course indefinitely
Automatically engage NAV on the alternate GPS receiver
Roll the wings level and default to basic roll mode (ROL)

explanation: AFM 4B.10.3 explains that losing the tracked navigation signal causes the autopilot to roll wings level and revert to ROL mode.

question: What is the permissible fuel imbalance in the AUXILIARY tanks (approved as acceptable) when the main tank imbalance is kept below 1 US gal?

options.text: An imbalance in the auxiliary tanks is approved under this condition
No auxiliary tank imbalance is ever approved
The auxiliary tanks must always be within 1 US gal of each other regardless of main tank balance
Auxiliary imbalance is approved only above 10,000 ft

explanation: AFM 4B.11 states that an imbalance in the auxiliary tanks is approved as long as the imbalance in the MAIN tanks stays below 1 US gal (3.8 liters), managed via CROSSFEED.

question: What is the maximum permissible fuel imbalance between the LH and RH MAIN tanks during an auxiliary fuel transfer fault?

options.text: 0.5 US gal (1.9 liters)
1 US gal (3.8 liters)
5 US gal (18.9 liters)
13.2 US gal (50 liters)

explanation: AFM 4B.11 gives the permissible main-tank imbalance limit as 1 US gal (3.8 liters), maintained using the CROSSFEED function.
